cultural.vision_reason: This is a Persian-style album painting depicting Persian costume conventions (turban with feather, robe styles), though the caption identifies the couple as being from Bukhara — a neighboring Central Asian culture whose dress and album-painting genre closely parallel Persian practice, and the work itself is a Persian miniature (Persian inscriptions, Persian painting idiom) from a Persian costume album. The style, medium, and production context are Persian court/costume painting, so it fits the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: album; painting
physical.summary:
Double portrait of a man and woman from Bukhara; single-page painting on an album folio. The man on the right kneels while presenting the lady, opposite on the left, with a flower. The bearded man wears a turban with a feather protruding, has a daggar hanging from the sash tied around his waist, and only one hand. The lady, gazing ambivelantly towards the viewer, wears a long coat over dress and pants, with hair covered by long shawl. Inscribed. Album contains 44 paintings and drawings, mostly of Persian costumes and animals with some drawings by Kaempfer.
Ink and opaque watercolour on paper. Album is bound in brown leather with gold gilt  decoration. Inside covers have marbled paper.
